def: High-bandwidth memory: the large off-chip memory on a GPU (80 GB on an H100) where weights and activations live between operations.
The number of floating-point operations an algorithm performs per byte it moves to and from main memory.
The arithmetic intensity at which a chip's peak FLOP/s and peak memory bandwidth are equally limiting, about 295 FLOP per byte for an H100 in bf16.
Describes an operation whose run time is set by how fast data can be moved, because its arithmetic intensity is below the chip's ridge point.
Describes an operation whose run time is set by arithmetic throughput, because its arithmetic intensity is above the chip's ridge point.
A function that runs on the GPU across many threads, launched from the CPU.
A single kernel that performs several operations while values stay on chip, avoiding writes and re-reads of intermediate arrays.
A plot of achievable FLOP/s against arithmetic intensity, bounded by a memory-bandwidth slope and a flat compute ceiling.
A Python-syntax language and compiler for writing GPU kernels in terms of blocks of values, with the compiler handling threads and shared memory.
PyTorch 2's compiler entry point, which captures a model as a graph and generates fused kernels, using Triton on GPUs.
